source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 7 (Composition and Structure of Atmosphere).

sections.heading: 1. Composition of the Atmosphere
points: The atmosphere is a mixture of **gases, water vapour and dust particles**.
**Gases:** **Nitrogen (~78%)** and **Oxygen (~21%)** dominate; plus **Argon, Carbon dioxide** and trace gases.
**Carbon dioxide** — vital for photosynthesis and the **greenhouse effect** (traps heat); increasing due to human activity.
**Ozone** (in the stratosphere) filters harmful **UV rays**; **water vapour** varies (decreases with altitude/latitude) and drives weather.

sections.heading: 2. Structure — Layers (by temperature)
points: **Troposphere** — lowest (up to ~8–18 km); all weather occurs here; temperature **decreases with height** (normal lapse rate ~6.5°C/km); ends at the **tropopause**.
**Stratosphere** — up to ~50 km; contains the **ozone layer**; temperature **rises** (ozone absorbs UV); stable — used by jet aircraft.
**Mesosphere** — up to ~80 km; temperature **falls** (coldest, ~-90°C at mesopause); meteors burn here.
**Thermosphere/Ionosphere** — temperature rises sharply; **ionised layers reflect radio waves**; auroras occur.
**Exosphere** — outermost, merges with space.

sections.heading: 3. Importance
points: The atmosphere sustains **life** (oxygen), protects from **UV (ozone)** and meteors, and keeps Earth **warm (greenhouse effect)**.
It is the medium of **weather and climate**.
It filters incoming solar radiation and retains outgoing heat.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Nitrogen ~78%, Oxygen ~21% (dominant gases).
Layers (bottom-up): Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere → Exosphere.
Troposphere = all weather; temperature falls with height (lapse rate ~6.5°C/km).
Stratosphere = ozone layer (absorbs UV; temperature rises).
Ionosphere (thermosphere) reflects radio waves; mesosphere is coldest (mesopause).

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **All weather occurs in the troposphere**; temperature **falls** with height there.
The **ozone layer is in the stratosphere** (where temperature rises).
The **mesosphere** is the **coldest** layer (mesopause).
The **ionosphere reflects radio waves** (aiding communication).
